answers.explanation: A hub is a layer 1 repeater: it never reads the frame.
Only one can transmit at a time, so collisions grow with the number of hosts.
Bridges and switches are layer 2 devices: they forward by MAC address.
Bridges and switches only know the MAC addresses on their own segments. Routers move traffic between networks.
It notes the source MAC and the port it came in on.
Flooding makes sure it reaches the destination. The reply then teaches the switch where that host is.
The destination already heard the frame on that segment.
A switch floods broadcasts out of every port. The switched LAN is one broadcast domain, unless it's split with VLANs or a router.
A virtual LAN. Frames between switches carry an 802.1Q tag with the VLAN ID.
L2TP carries the traffic; IPsec encrypts it.
